intro: The offline-sync plan for the Notebook app. Approve, change or skip each piece, pick the settings layout, and answer the open questions. Build opens once nothing is left on Change and every question is answered.

status.label: Round 1 · awaiting your approval · nothing has been built

notes_answered.note: What happens when two devices edit the same note?
notes_answered.answer: The newer edit wins per paragraph and the older one is kept as a conflict copy. See the revised piece.
I turned this into a question with a recommendation, since it changes storage size.
Option B now puts it on the main settings page. Worth a second look.

items.title: Offline first
items.quote: I want to write on the train without a signal.
items.rule: Every edit is saved on the device first and synced later; nothing waits on the network.

items.title: No accounts in this plan
items.quote: Keep sign-in out of it for now.
items.rule: Sync uses the existing device pairing; account work is listed under Later.

items.title: Same look as today
items.rule: No visual redesign: new controls reuse the current settings components.

blocks.title: How I read the rest
blocks.text: Where the brief was silent, I assumed the following. Approve to keep them, or Change with a note.
items: Sync runs every 5 minutes and on app open, never on a metered connection unless allowed.
Attachments over 20 MB sync only on Wi-Fi.
A failed sync retries with backoff and shows a quiet badge, not a dialog.

blocks.title: How long should deleted notes stay recoverable?
blocks.text: Longer history costs device storage; shorter history risks losing something.

recommendation.why: Matches what most note apps do and keeps storage bounded.

blocks.answer: It is the common default; pick a different number if your notes need longer.

blocks.title: Should sync pause on low battery?

recommendation.why: Sync is the biggest background cost; the next charge catches up.

blocks.title: Local change log
blocks.text: Record every edit on the device in an append-only log, so nothing depends on the network.

blocks.title: Conflict handling
blocks.text: When two devices edit the same note, the newer edit wins per paragraph and the older version is kept as a conflict copy.
items: Conflict copies are named with the device and time
A banner on the note links to its copy

blocks.asked: What happens when two devices edit the same note?
blocks.answer: Paragraph-level merge, with the older text kept as a conflict copy instead of being dropped.

blocks.title: Sync status in settings
blocks.text: A row in settings shows the last sync time and a Sync now button.
